record_type_quote: Cohen and Jones (2008) have suggested that individuals who draw poorly have problems in the perception of objects, so that the extent of shape constancy (phenomenal regression) correlates with drawing ability, there being a “robust negative relation between perceptual errors resulting from shape constancy and drawing accuracy.” The present article describes two attempts to replicate that finding, with 30 non-art students in Study 1 and with 106 art students in Study 2.

targets.authors: Cohen D. J., & Jones H. E.
targets.title: How shape constancy relates to drawing accuracy.
targets.evidence_quote: Cohen and Jones (2008) have suggested that individuals who draw poorly have problems in the perception of objects, so that the extent of shape constancy (phenomenal regression) correlates with drawing ability, there being a “robust negative relation between perceptual errors resulting from shape constancy and drawing accuracy.” The present article describes two attempts to replicate that finding, with 30 non-art students in Study 1 and with 106 art students in Study 2.
targets.outcome_quote: Study 1 found a correlation that was statistically significant, but in the opposite direction to that reported by Cohen and Jones, and in Study 2 the correlation was very close to zero.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Both attempts failed to confirm the specific negative correlation: one reversed direction and the other was near zero. The title also explicitly identifies two failures.
